about: Language-neutral conformance fixture for the ContactLogo matching engine. Every case is decidable offline from docs/ENGINE-CONTRACT.md with no network access. ContactLogoKit (Swift), web/src/engine (TypeScript) and Apps/ContactLogoAndroid (Kotlin) must all produce the same answer for every case.

contact.emails: string[] — full addresses, in contact order
contact.websites: string[] — raw URL field values, in contact order, any scheme
contact.phones: string[] — raw phone strings, in contact order
contact.hasImage: boolean — the contact already has a photo

expect.query: string | null — the brand query. null for person and nonBrand: no lookup is performed (ENGINE-CONTRACT R7.6)
expect.domain: string | null — resolved registrable domain. null when class is not businessCard, or when no identity resolved
expect.via: website | email | catalog | phone | guess | null
expect.maxConfidence: skip | low | medium | high — the STATIC CEILING (ENGINE-CONTRACT R10). The final tier is min(staticCeiling, assetTier); an engine must never exceed this value for this contact, whatever assets come back
expect.flags: string[] — the complete set of STATIC flags (ENGINE-CONTRACT R12.1). Compare as a set, order-insensitive. Asset-time flags (favicon-fallback, fallback-tile, domain-match, non-square, aggregator-source, name-mismatch) are never asserted here
expect.simpleIconsSlug: OPTIONAL string | null — the Simple Icons slug for expect.domain (ENGINE-CONTRACT R13). null means no Simple Icons candidate may be emitted. Absent means the case does not assert it

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §1 non-brand, §4 generic nouns; ENGINE-CONTRACT R7.1
cases.why: A generic noun on the exact blocklist; a red-cross clip-art is worse than no logo.
GENERIC exact match — never a brand, never in the not-found bucket.
A role, not an organization.
Parenthetical is stripped first, then NON_BRAND /\bverification\b/ matches; a Twilio logo here would be wrong.
NON_BRAND is tested before any ' at ' brand-tail split, so this never becomes a query for 'Farm'.
NON_BRAND pattern /\bpassword\b/ — a service SMS sender, not a brand.
From the battle-test blocklist — matched unrelated medical clip-art.
'jerry' is in both GENERIC and HOMONYM. GENERIC is tested first, so the contact is skipped, not matched at medium.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §4 generic nouns; ENGINE-CONTRACT R7.1 precedence
cases.why: Same GENERIC-before-HOMONYM precedence as 'Jerry'.
Carrier-generated label, not an organization.
Role head is dropped, leaving 'Hospital', which the post-segment GENERIC re-check catches.
Given/family present and no brand tail — never a logo target.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §1 'Employees are not the company', §5 rule 7; ENGINE-CONTRACT R7.3
cases.why: A person with a corporate email is an employee; the Apple logo must not land on her card.
Display name is a person and the only email is freemail — organization alone never promotes a person.
Role junk in `organization` is irrelevant: a person with a photo is photo-protected, not 'not found'.
Control for the rule-8 case below: without a brand tail this is just a person.
The tail is a role, so rule 8 does not fire and the contact stays a person.
The lone-firm-name promotion is blocked by a consumer email address — this is a human who happens to be filed oddly.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §1 business card, §2b step 3; ENGINE-CONTRACT R8.3
cases.why: The canonical easy case: no person name, unambiguous catalog brand, iconic mark available.
Store-location parentheticals are stripped before any lookup.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §1 business-card example; ENGINE-CONTRACT R8.3 CATALOG_TAIL_OK
cases.why: The rulebook's own business-card example: a catalog head plus a department tail resolves to the parent brand.
Catalog head match with a locationish tail; the query keeps the full name, only the domain reduces.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §2b 'A lone given or family name that is a catalog firm'; ENGINE-CONTRACT R7.4
cases.why: A catalog firm parked in the given-name field is a business card, not a person.
A contact-owned website is the strongest identity evidence and can reach high; no Simple Icons slug exists, so none may be invented.
A non-freemail work address is contact-owned evidence and may reach high.
'Reservations' is not a catalog tail, so resolution falls through to the published customer-service number.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §1 'replace-existing caps at medium', §6; ENGINE-CONTRACT R10.4
cases.why: Overwriting an existing photo always goes through review, never pre-checked.
When `organization` is present it is the brand source, so a generic display name does not blocklist the card.
shop.walgreens.com must reduce to walgreens.com, or the catalog entry and the Simple Icons glyph are both missed.
Reduces to the registrable domain, but 'UT Austin Registrar' shares no token with 'utexas', so R10.1b caps it at medium rather than pre-checking.
co.uk is a two-label public suffix, so three labels are kept — reducing to co.uk would be catastrophic.
Path and query string must be discarded before the host is reduced.
www. is stripped but is not a reduction, so `subdomain-reduced` must not be emitted.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §4 junk domains ('doug@texasdescon.com as URL'); ENGINE-CONTRACT R1.4
cases.why: An email address typed into the URL field still carries the right domain once userinfo is stripped.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §4 junk domains ('only http(s) URLs'); ENGINE-CONTRACT R1.2
cases.why: A non-web scheme yields no identity, so resolution falls through to the capped guess.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §4 junk domains ('strip social/profile domains'); ENGINE-CONTRACT R3 (CL-03)
cases.why: The audit's exact reproduction: a LinkedIn company page must never resolve to linkedin.com or produce the LinkedIn glyph pre-checked.
Small businesses whose only web presence is a Facebook page are the common case for this trap.
Yelp is on the canonical SOCIAL set; the web engine currently has no social set at all.
Social hosts are skipped, not fatal: the next website in contact order is used and can still reach high.

cases.rule: ENGINE-CONTRACT R3.2 (SOCIAL applies to the email path too)
cases.why: A social host in the email field is as wrong a logo source as one in the URL field.
wixsite.com serves the Wix favicon for every tenant — the same failure class as CL-03.

cases.rule: ENGINE-CONTRACT R3.3 (the full host is tested, not only the registrable domain)
cases.why: Reducing sites.google.com to google.com would put the Google logo on a little-league team, so the host is rejected before reduction and resolution falls through to the capped guess.
gmail.com must never become a logo domain.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §4 junk domains ('gnail.com typos'); ENGINE-CONTRACT R2
cases.why: Freemail typo-squats are on the canonical FREEMAIL set so they never resolve as a brand.
The guess path must use companyKey(): with 'LLC' left on, the slug is 27 chars, trips the 24-char cap and the contact vanishes.
Paired with the LLC case: the two must be indistinguishable in domain, via, ceiling and flags.

cases.rule: ENGINE-CONTRACT R5.2 (LEGAL_SUFFIX allows a leading comma)
cases.why: ', Inc.' is the most common written form and must strip identically to ' LLC'.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §4 homonyms; ENGINE-CONTRACT R4.5 (HOMONYM is keyed on companyKey)
cases.why: Homonym lookup must use companyKey, or 'Apple Inc' escapes the cap that 'Apple' gets.

cases.rule: ENGINE-CONTRACT R5.2 (the legal suffix must be a separate token)
cases.why: The shipping regex starts with `\s*,?\s*`, all of which can match empty, so the `co` alternative eats the end of the word: companyKey('Cisco') is 'cis' today and the catalog entry is unreachable. Same defect hides Costco and lets Medico past the blocklist.
Paired with the Cisco case; 'Costco' must not normalize to 'cost'.
Users type 'H & R Block', 'H&R Block' and 'H and R Block'; all three must reach the same catalog entry.

cases.rule: ENGINE-CONTRACT R8.5 ('&' expands to 'and' in the guess slug)
cases.why: '&' is not a legal DNS character; the canonical expansion is 'and', not deletion.
Stripping hyphens from the key would break 7-eleven, t-mobile, h-e-b and buc-ees at once.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE section 1 (Person: never a logo target); section 5 rule 8 as scoped to org-only cards
cases.why: The rulebook's own rule-8 example, and it has givenName Byron / familyName Goode. Section 1 outranks it: this is a person who sells insurance, not Root Insurance. MATCHING-ENGINE section 1: a contact with a given or family name is a Person, 'never a logo target — employees are not the company'. The display name's brand tail says who this person is affiliated with, not that the card is that business. Section 5 rule 8 applies only to a card with no name fields.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE section 1 (Person: never a logo target); section 5 rule 8 as scoped to org-only cards
cases.why: The 'X At Y' form says plainly that Chris works at NTB. Section 5 rule 7 calls that an employee contact; section 1 says employees are not the company. MATCHING-ENGINE section 1: a contact with a given or family name is a Person, 'never a logo target — employees are not the company'. The display name's brand tail says who this person is affiliated with, not that the card is that business. Section 5 rule 8 applies only to a card with no name fields.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE section 1 (Person: never a logo target); section 5 rule 8 as scoped to org-only cards
cases.why: Same 'X At Y' form with a catalog brand. Dana is a person; Costco's mark on her card is the wrong-logo outcome the product exists to prevent. MATCHING-ENGINE section 1: a contact with a given or family name is a Person, 'never a logo target — employees are not the company'. The display name's brand tail says who this person is affiliated with, not that the card is that business. Section 5 rule 8 applies only to a card with no name fields.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §5 rule 7 beats rule 8; ENGINE-CONTRACT R7.3.b
cases.why: When the contact's own email domain equals the tail's resolved domain, the person works there — rule 8 must not fire.
Rule 8 is not limited to person heads: a franchise-style 'local name - brand' entry queries the brand tail, capped at medium.
The rulebook's own trap: the undecorated query is the parent brand, and 'Apple' is a homonym with no contact-owned domain, so it stays at medium.
A locationish tail after ' - ' is decoration, not a brand tail.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §1 notes ('organization often contains role junk'); ENGINE-CONTRACT R6.3
cases.why: The rulebook's own role-junk example; the role tail is removed before lookup.
Second role-junk example from the rulebook, reached through the same ROLE_WORDS list.
A generic word in the tail is decoration on a real business, not a reason to blocklist the whole card.
Bank, car marque or planet — with no contact context this can never auto-apply. Its only likely asset is a favicon, which is itself capped at medium.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §4 ('use contact context as a category signal'); ENGINE-CONTRACT R10.2
cases.why: Contact-owned evidence resolves the homonym, so the cap lifts while the flag stays for the review UI.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §4 homonyms, §3 source 1; ENGINE-CONTRACT R10.2 + R13.3
cases.why: A catalog hit is name-derived, not contact context, so it does not resolve a homonym. simpleIconsSlug is null: delta.com is on the Simple Icons SKIP set because the 'delta' slug is the software company, and slugs must never be derived from the domain.
Same contact name, contact-owned domain: the cap lifts, but the Simple Icons skip still applies.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §2b ordering; ENGINE-CONTRACT R8.3 before R8.4
cases.why: Catalog is step 3 and phone is step 4, so the catalog wins the `via` label even though the phone agrees — ordering must be identical in all three engines.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §4 homonyms ('IBC = International Bank of Commerce ≠ IBC Root Beer')
cases.why: The rulebook's headline homonym; a guessed domain plus homonym risk is doubly capped.
The qualifier changes the companyKey to 'ibc bank', which is not a homonym, and the work email is contact-owned.
United Airlines, United Rentals, United Way — the catalog answer is a guess dressed up, so it stays in review.
Contact-owned domain lifts the homonym cap; the flag remains so the review UI can explain the risk.
Two independent caps land on the same contact; the result is still exactly medium, not low.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §4 brand vs parent; ENGINE-CONTRACT R8.3
cases.why: The consumer-facing fuel brand keeps its own catalog entry and must not be folded into the corporate parent.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §4 brand vs parent; ENGINE-CONTRACT R8.3
cases.why: Paired with 'Exxon': the two names must not collapse onto one domain.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §4 domain redirect after merger; ENGINE-CONTRACT R10.5
cases.why: ntb.com now serves Mavis Tire, so even a contact-owned domain is capped at medium; the domain-derived logo may be the successor brand.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §2 rule 4 alias map; ENGINE-CONTRACT R8.3
cases.why: Alias entries live in the catalog, so a three-letter abbreviation resolves without a guess.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §2 rule 4 alias map; ENGINE-CONTRACT R8.3
cases.why: The second rulebook alias; without the catalog this would guess gcx.com and be wrong.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §4 fallback tiles, §6; ENGINE-CONTRACT R8.5 + R11.4 (CL-18)
cases.why: The audit's invented brand. A guessed domain is capped at medium, and any letter-tile asset returned for it must be rejected by isFallbackTile before it can be offered at all.

contact.displayName: Northwest Harris County Municipal Utility District

expect.query: Northwest Harris County Municipal Utility District

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §2b step 5; ENGINE-CONTRACT R8.5 (3–24 character cap)
cases.why: Long descriptive names produce absurd guesses; the engine refuses rather than inventing a domain.
Two-character names are almost never a resolvable brand; skip rather than guess.
Every earlier step is disqualified (junk scheme, freemail, no catalog, non-toll-free local number), so the capped guess is the only route left.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE §4 homonyms; ENGINE-CONTRACT R8.3 (CATALOG_TAIL_OK excludes trade words)
cases.why: 'Dental' is not a location or sub-brand tail, so the catalog must NOT fold this onto delta.com and hand it the airline logo.
The slug is not the domain label: deriving 'chase' from chase.com yields no icon at all.
att.com maps to the 'atandt' slug; TLD-stripping would request a non-existent 'att' icon.
An unmapped domain yields no Simple Icons candidate; deriving one requests a 404 or, worse, an unrelated brand's mark.
A street name is not on any word list and never will be. The tail is marked as an address by 'rd'; 'mason' is simply unrecognised, which is not a reason to refuse the parent brand.

cases.rule: ENGINE-CONTRACT R8.3 CATALOG_TAIL_OK; MATCHING-ENGINE section 4 disambiguation
cases.why: The trap one word from the contract's own 'Delta Dental' example. 'center' is a place word, so any-word matching handed a dental practice Delta Air Lines' logo. A trade word in the tail makes it a different business, so the head brand must not be reduced to.
'bakery' is on both SUBBRAND_TAIL and ORG_SIGNAL. The department list wins: an H-E-B bakery counter is H-E-B.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE section 1 (Person: never a logo target); section 5 rule 8 as scoped to org-only cards
cases.why: An unrelated work email does not turn a named person into a business. The employee guard's own mechanism was wrong (it compared the email with itself), but the outcome it produced here was right. MATCHING-ENGINE section 1: a contact with a given or family name is a Person, 'never a logo target — employees are not the company'. The display name's brand tail says who this person is affiliated with, not that the card is that business. Section 5 rule 8 applies only to a card with no name fields.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE section 5 rule 7 beats rule 8; ENGINE-CONTRACT R7.3.b
cases.why: The other side of the same guard, so a fix cannot simply disable it: an email at the brand on the card does mean a person who works there, and rule 7 wins.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE section 1 (Person: never a logo target); section 5 rule 8 as scoped to org-only cards
cases.why: No email at all, and still a person: the classification comes from the name fields, not from what contact details happen to exist. MATCHING-ENGINE section 1: a contact with a given or family name is a Person, 'never a logo target — employees are not the company'. The display name's brand tail says who this person is affiliated with, not that the card is that business. Section 5 rule 8 applies only to a card with no name fields.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE section 1 (Person: never a logo target); section 5 rule 8 scoped to org-only cards
cases.why: Classification keyed on name fields alone leaves a hole: a vCard carrying only FN and no N parses with no givenName, so this card would be a business and wear Costco's mark. The head of the split reads as a person's name, which settles it without a name field.

cases.rule: MATCHING-ENGINE section 1 (Person: never a logo target); section 5 rule 8 scoped to org-only cards
cases.why: The other side of the same test, and the reason the head is read rather than the 'At' form suppressed outright: a pharmacy counter inside a Costco is a real department and should carry the brand. 'Pharmacy' is an ORG_SIGNAL trade word, so the head is not personal.
